Jobs::RetrieveTopic has no spec at all despite containing validation logic (InvalidParameters on blank embed_url, user lookup, staff no_throttle propagation)

Controller spec missing referer-mismatch edge case: no test that a referer from a different host is rejected, nor for unparseable referer triggering the URI::InvalidURIError rescue in ensure_embeddable
Disqus import task switched from PostCreator to TopicEmbed.import_remote (and dropped --category option) with no test covering the new path

Raw HTML cook path renders unsanitized external content: Post#cook short-circuits to return raw for raw_html posts, bypassing sanitization, and TopicEmbed.import feeds arbitrary external HTML into PostCreator with skip_validations: true, enabling stored XSS on the forum and embedded pages
CGI.unescapeHTML on feed content in PollFeed re-activates entity-escaped HTML, converting <script> back into <script> and acting as an XSS amplifier while corrupting legitimate content
PollFeed crashes with NoMethodError on feed items lacking content (i.content.scrub), and with retry: false one malformed item silently aborts the entire poll
PostRevisor gains a global skip_validations option that changes the public contract of revise! for all callers, letting any caller passing skip_validations in its opts hash silently skip validation
Post#cook early return bypasses Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...), silently voiding plugin guarantees for raw_html posts
Host-validation logic is duplicated across EmbedController, TopicRetriever, PollFeed, and TopicEmbed with inconsistent implementations that will drift
TopicRetriever synchronously executes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}), bypassing Sidekiq and coupling the retriever to the poller's internals; should use Jobs.enqueue or extracted shared logic
Non-atomic Redis setnx/expire in TopicRetriever can leave a key with no TTL if the process dies between calls, permanently wedging retrieval for that embed URL; should use SET key val EX 60 NX
Dead code: Jobs::PollFeed#feed_key and its require 'digest/sha1' are never called
Dead locale key embed.permalink is added but never referenced by any view or JS
TopicEmbed.import mutates its contents argument in place with <<, a hidden side effect on a public model API

TopicEmbed.import bakes the localized footer HTML into content_sha1, so translation changes trigger mass rewrites of embedded posts and the hash no longer represents source content; the unescaped URL interpolation is also an injection point
Already-applied migrations edited in the same PR (whitespace/newline changes and force: true added to create_top_topics), causing schema divergence and silent table drops on replay
Weak postMessage origin check in embed.js uses substring indexOf match instead of strict origin comparison
embed.js dereferences document.getElementById('discourse-comments') without a null check, throwing on pages where the div is missing
`force: true` added to already-shipped migration create_top_topics, causing destructive DROP TABLE re-run risk
`force: true` on new topic_embeds table converts 'already exists' error into silent data destruction on re-run
NOT NULL column with default added to large posts table without concurrency safeguards, causing table rewrite and ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock downtime
content_sha1 updated unconditionally even when revision fails, permanently losing content updates for feed imports
Feed items without content crash the entire poll_feed job, skipping all remaining items
Double-HTML-decoding of feed content with raw_html cook method enables raw HTML injection into posts
Non-atomic SETNX/EXPIRE throttle in topic_retriever can permanently blacklist an embed URL if process dies between calls
Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript in embed layout, allowing broken JS or script injection
Removal of --category option from Disqus import is a breaking interface change with no deprecation path
PollFeed#feed_key is dead code — no ETag/Last-Modified conditional-GET tracking implemented

Stored XSS: Post#cook returns raw verbatim when cook_method == raw_html, and TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method: raw_html from unsanitized feed content, rendered via <%= raw post.cooked %> in the embed view

PollFeed only does CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) with no tag filtering or attribute stripping, and unescapeHTML re-animates correctly escaped payloads like <script> into live markup before storing raw

HTML/attribute injection in the 'imported from' footer: url is interpolated into a single-quoted HTML attribute with no escaping; the /^https?\:\/\// guard is trivially bypassed by payloads like http://evil.com/' onmouseover='alert(1)
PollFeed crashes on feeds lacking content:encoded (plain RSS description-only or many Atom feeds) because i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError, with no fallback to i.description/i.summary
No per-item rescue in PollFeed's rss.items.each: the first malformed entry aborts the loop, so items after it are silently skipped every hour with retry: false and no logging

Referer-based validation in embed_controller is trivially spoofable, allowing anonymous users to hit /embed/best?embed_url=... for unlimited URLs, each enqueueing a RetrieveTopic job (job-queue flooding and request-amplification DoS against the embeddable host)

SSRF in import_remote/PollFeed: open(url) follows redirects with no scheme/IP validation and no DNS rebinding protection, allowing rebinding to internal addresses (e.g., 169.254.169.254) and exfiltration via imported content
No read timeout or response-size cap on remote fetches, so a slow-drip server can pin a Sidekiq worker indefinitely

Non-atomic SETNX+EXPIRE in TopicRetriever: if the process dies between setnx and expire, the key persists with no TTL forever, permanently blocking retrieval for that URL; should use atomic SET key val NX EX 60
content_sha1 is updated via update_column even when revisor.revise! fails (return value ignored), silently marking the embed as synced when the post diverges from the source

Silent no-op when embed_by_username doesn't resolve: both poll_feed and fetch_http do 'return if user.blank?' with no logging, so a typo'd username causes the system to run green while importing nothing

loading.html.erb reloads the iframe every 30 seconds indefinitely even when retrieval can never succeed (host mismatch, unset embed_by_username, permanent fetch failure), creating an infinite job-churn amplifier
embed_url column is t.string (255 chars) with a unique index, but real-world URLs routinely exceed 255 characters, causing TopicEmbed.create! to raise and abort remaining PollFeed items
Dependency lock incomplete: only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated; the primary Gemfile.lock is not, so frozen-mode deployments or CI against the main lockfile will fail or miss the new gems

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded feed import in PollFeed#poll_feed: rss.items.each imports every item with no cap, causing long-running jobs that hog Sidekiq slots and hammer the DB

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, PollFeed#poll_feed does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items.each` importing every item via `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no explicit cap, batching, or early-exit based on recency. This means the job’s runtime and DB/write load are proportional to the feed size returned, which can be very large, leading to long-running scheduled jobs that can tie up Sidekiq workers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Synchronous full feed poll inside retrieve path: perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously, blocking workers while processing the entire feed instead of just the single embed URL

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `perform_retrieve` contains:

```rb
if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?
  Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})
  return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?
end
```

`Jobs::PollFeed#execute` calls `poll_feed`, which does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items.each` importing every item. This is a full-feed fetch+process performed synchronously inside the retrieve path (invoked by `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`), so it will block that worker/job while the entire feed is processed, even though the retriever is for a single `@embed_url`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: open(url) calls with no timeout or size limit in topic_embed.rb import_remote and poll_feed.rb, reading entire response into memory and pinning workers on slow remote hosts

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces remote fetches using Ruby's open-uri without any explicit timeouts or response size limits. In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb it does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, and in app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote it does `open(url).read`. Both can block a Sidekiq worker on slow/unresponsive hosts and can read arbitrarily large responses fully into memory (`.read` in particular), making the risk of resource exhaustion verifiable from the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Job enqueue per request with no dedup/coalescing in embed_controller: every /embed/best request for a missing TopicEmbed enqueues a RetrieveTopic job, and failed imports cause indefinite job churn with no negative-result caching

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns nil, it unconditionally enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...). There is no deduplication/coalescing at enqueue time, and the loading view auto-reloads every 30 seconds, causing repeated /embed/best requests and thus repeated enqueues while the embed is still missing. Although TopicRetriever has a 60s Redis throttle (retrieved_recently?) to reduce repeated fetch attempts, it does not prevent the queue from filling with redundant RetrieveTopic jobs, and there is no negative-result caching if retrieval keeps failing (network/user missing/etc.), so repeated requests can cause ongoing job enqueue churn.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic setnx/expire in topic_retriever.rb can leak a permanent throttle key with no TTL if the process dies between calls; should use SET key val NX EX 60

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, retrieved_recently? implements throttling with two separate Redis calls: `if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. Because these are not atomic, if the process/thread crashes or is killed after the SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE runs, the key can be left without a TTL, causing the embed URL to be throttled indefinitely. This matches the proposed finding; using a single atomic command (e.g., SET key val NX EX 60) would avoid the permanent-key risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feed re-processed in full every hour with no conditional GET (ETag/Last-Modified); feed_key is dead code, causing wasted full fetch/parse/lookup work on unchanged feeds

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the scheduled job runs `hourly` and `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no use of HTTP conditional caching headers (ETag/Last-Modified) or any stored “last seen” marker, so it will fetch and parse the entire feed every run. Also, the `feed_key` method (which computes a Redis key based on the feed URL) is defined but never referenced anywhere in the diff, so it is dead code and not actually used to avoid reprocessing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Revision churn when feed content changes trivially: volatile RSS fragments (timestamps, ad slots) trigger a PostRevisor revision per item per hour, growing post_revisions and re-indexing continuously

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, every hourly run re-imports each RSS item and calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`. `TopicEmbed.import` computes `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` and, for existing embeds, calls `PostRevisor#revise!` whenever the SHA differs, then updates `embed.content_sha1`. Because the SHA is over the full `contents` string (plus the appended "Imported from" footer), any trivial/volatile change in the feed-provided HTML (ads, timestamps, tracking params, minor markup differences) will cause a revision on each poll. This can lead to continuous post revision creation and downstream work (e.g., re-cooking/reindexing) with no mitigation in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No timeouts (open_timeout/read_timeout) on outbound HTTP calls in poll_feed.rb and topic_embed.rb, allowing remote servers to hang Sidekiq workers indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds multiple outbound HTTP fetches using `open-uri` without specifying `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`: in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` (`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and in `app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote` (`Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`). These are invoked from Sidekiq jobs (`Jobs::PollFeed`, `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` via `TopicRetriever`), so a slow/hung remote endpoint (or DNS/connect stall not covered by defaults) can tie up a worker for an unbounded/very long time. The absence of explicit timeouts is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RetrieveTopic job has no retry control or error handling, causing permanent failures to be retried 25 times over ~20 days
One malformed feed item aborts the entire poll run in PollFeed due to NoMethodError on missing content or nil URL, with no rescue around the per-item loop
Redis throttle key in topic_retriever.rb set with non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE can be left without a TTL, permanently blocking retrieval

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two distinct Redis commands; if the process crashes or loses the Redis connection after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE is issued (or EXPIRE fails), the key will be created without a TTL. Since subsequent calls will see SETNX return false, retrieval will be throttled indefinitely for that embed_url. This is a real correctness/availability issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loading page reloads forever with no circuit breaker when topic retrieval never succeeds, causing unbounded client reloads and job churn

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when no topic exists it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `embed/loading`. The `loading.html.erb` view unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds with no max-attempts/circuit breaker. If retrieval never succeeds (e.g., remote fetch fails, settings wrong, parsing errors), the iframe will reload forever and each reload will enqueue another `retrieve_topic` job. Although `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles *work* to once per 60s, it does not prevent the controller from continuously enqueuing jobs, so this can cause ongoing reloads and unnecessary job queue churn.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve runs the full feed poll synchronously inside a job, blocking a worker for the duration of a full feed poll

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it directly calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (synchronously) before doing `fetch_http`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all `rss.items`, importing each one. Since `TopicRetriever#retrieve` is invoked from the Sidekiq job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute`, this means a regular worker can end up running a full feed poll inline and be occupied for the duration of that network fetch + item processing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import update path updates content_sha1 unconditionally even if revision didn't apply, causing future updates of the same content to be silently skipped

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an embed already exists and `content_sha1` differs, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then immediately does `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` without checking whether `revise!` actually succeeded/returned true. Since `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (it explicitly `return false if not should_revise?`), the code can record the new SHA1 even if the post wasn’t updated, causing subsequent imports of the same content to be skipped because the SHA1 now matches while the stored post content may not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls can raise URI::InvalidURIError despite the regex pre-check, since the validation and URI parsing disagree about valid URLs

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` only pre-checks `url` with `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, but then calls `absolutize_urls(url, contents)` which does `uri = URI(url)` with no rescue. Many strings can match the regex while still being rejected by `URI()` (e.g., containing spaces or other invalid characters in the path/query), which would raise `URI::InvalidURIError` and crash the import/polling flow. The diff shows no exception handling around `URI(url)` in `absolutize_urls`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Resize postMessage uses interpolated request.referer as targetOrigin, throwing a SyntaxError in browsers when Referer is missing so the iframe never resizes
embed.js assumes #discourse-comments element exists, throwing a TypeError and silently failing if the host page omits the div

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the script does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe)`. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and `appendChild` will throw a `TypeError` at runtime, preventing the embed from working.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller 'success' specs in embed_controller_spec.rb mock out the entire system under test, verifying mock wiring instead of real behavior; no request/integration spec exercises embed/best end-to-end with a real TopicView

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds controller specs for `EmbedController#best` that intentionally stub `SiteSetting`, `request.referer`, and expectations on `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed`, `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`, and `TopicView.new(...)`. While these are mock-heavy unit/controller tests, this is a test design/coverage critique rather than a verifiable defect (bug/security/correctness issue) introduced by the code. Nothing in the diff indicates the endpoint is incorrect solely because there is no end-to-end/integration spec exercising a real `TopicView` render.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Job enqueue contract is untested: spec stubs TopicRetriever.new instead of asserting Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) with correct embed_url and user_id, and only passes due to inline job execution in test environment

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no topic_id is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` under "tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found" does not assert `Jobs.enqueue` is called; instead it expects `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve`, which the controller does not invoke directly. This means the spec is not actually testing the controller’s enqueue behavior or the job args (embed_url/user_id), and could pass only if enqueue executes the job immediately in the test environment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed core logic (RSS parsing, i.link/i.id fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML, user lookup, TopicEmbed.import) has zero coverage; untested nil i.content.scrub would raise NoMethodError and kill the hourly poll

Redis throttle logic in TopicRetriever is never tested — tests stub retrieved_recently? itself, so the real $redis.setnx/expire throttle, key expiry, and no_throttle staff bypass are unexercised; perform_retrieve and fetch_http branches also have no coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicRetriever` with real throttle logic in `retrieved_recently?` that uses `$redis.setnx`/`expire` and a `no_throttle` bypass. However, the added spec (`spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb`) stubs `retrieved_recently?` itself in the “valid host” cases, so the redis-based throttling behavior, key expiry, and bypass are not exercised. Additionally, no specs cover `perform_retrieve`’s internal branches (existing `TopicEmbed` short-circuit, feed polling path, or `fetch_http`/`import_remote`). This is a verifiable lack of test coverage in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import update path doesn't verify embed.content_sha1 bookkeeping or the no-op case (unchanged content must not create a PostRevision); import_remote and non-80/443 port branch of absolutize_urls also untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s `TopicEmbed.import` update path correctly computes `content_sha1`, compares it to `embed.content_sha1`, and only revises the post + updates `content_sha1` when changed; when unchanged it’s a no-op. The proposed finding is primarily about missing/insufficient test coverage (no explicit spec for the unchanged-content no-revision case, `import_remote`, and the non-80/443 port branch in `absolutize_urls`), which is not itself a verifiable defect/bug introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostRevisor save-validation change (@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])) ships with no test verifying skip_validations persists an otherwise-invalid post and the default path still validates

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, which is a functional change, but it is not itself a defect; it makes the `skip_validations` option actually take effect (previously it was ignored). The proposed finding is about missing test coverage for this behavior. Lack of a specific test asserting “invalid post persists when skip_validations is true” is not a verifiable bug/correctness issue introduced by the diff, and the diff even adds/updates other specs (e.g., `TopicEmbed` update path) though they don’t specifically assert validation behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Jobs::RetrieveTopic has no spec at all despite containing validation logic (InvalidParameters on blank embed_url, user lookup, staff no_throttle propagation)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` and does not add any corresponding spec file for it, so the claim that it lacks tests is factually verifiable. However, “no spec” is not itself a bug/security/correctness defect in the code introduced by the diff; it’s a test coverage/process preference rather than a functional problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller spec missing referer-mismatch edge case: no test that a referer from a different host is rejected, nor for unparseable referer triggering the URI::InvalidURIError rescue in ensure_embeddable

adjudication.rationale: In the new `EmbedController`, `ensure_embeddable` rejects requests when `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and also rescues `URI::InvalidURIError` to raise `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. The added `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` covers: missing `embed_url`, missing `embeddable_host`, and the case where `referer` is nil. It does not include any test where `referer` is present but from a different host (mismatch rejection), nor a test where `referer` is an unparseable URI to exercise the `URI::InvalidURIError` rescue path. So the finding describes a real, verifiable test coverage gap in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import task switched from PostCreator to TopicEmbed.import_remote (and dropped --category option) with no test covering the new path

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `--category` option from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and changes the import implementation to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, and there are no tests added for the Thor task’s new behavior. However, the lack of tests for this task is not, by itself, a verifiable defect/bug introduced in the code (it’s a coverage/process concern), and the removal of the category option is an explicit behavior change that may be intentional; the diff does not provide evidence it is incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw HTML cook path renders unsanitized external content: Post#cook short-circuits to return raw for raw_html posts, bypassing sanitization, and TopicEmbed.import feeds arbitrary external HTML into PostCreator with skip_validations: true, enabling stored XSS on the forum and embedded pages

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum and changes `Post#cook` to immediately `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (where sanitization would typically occur). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts from externally sourced content (`contents` from RSS via `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and from `Readability::Document` over `open(url).read`) and passes it to `PostCreator` with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `skip_validations: true`. In the embed view, it renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and for `raw_html` posts `cooked == raw`, so any unsafe HTML/JS in the imported content would be stored and rendered. There is no sanitization step shown in this diff for the raw_html path, making stored XSS a verifiable risk introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CGI.unescapeHTML on feed content in PollFeed re-activates entity-escaped HTML, converting <script> back into <script> and acting as an XSS amplifier while corrupting legitimate content

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, feed item content is processed as `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then imported via `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore, if a feed provides entity-escaped HTML like `<script>...`, `CGI.unescapeHTML` will decode it into real tags, which are then stored and rendered as raw HTML, making this a verifiable XSS-enabling behavior introduced by the diff (and also potentially corrupting intentionally-escaped content).

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed crashes with NoMethodError on feed items lacking content (i.content.scrub), and with retry: false one malformed item silently aborts the entire poll
PostRevisor gains a global skip_validations option that changes the public contract of revise! for all callers, letting any caller passing skip_validations in its opts hash silently skip validation

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, adding support for an explicit `skip_validations` opt. This does not alter behavior for existing callers unless they *already* pass `skip_validations` (which is not shown), because the default remains to validate. In this diff, the only new usage is deliberate (`TopicEmbed.import` passes `skip_validations: true` when revising imported content). The finding frames this as a problematic “global/public contract change” that lets “any caller” bypass validations, but there’s no evidence in the diff of untrusted input reaching this option or of accidental bypass for existing callers; it appears to be an intentional internal feature addition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post#cook early return bypasses Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...), silently voiding plugin guarantees for raw_html posts

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now returns `raw` immediately when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which means the subsequent `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` call is skipped for those posts. Since TopicEmbed.import creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html`, any plugins relying on the `:after_post_cook` hook will not run for embedded/imported posts, a concrete behavioral change introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host-validation logic is duplicated across EmbedController, TopicRetriever, PollFeed, and TopicEmbed with inconsistent implementations that will drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows host checking in two places with different purposes: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` validates the **request referer host** against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, while `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` validates the **embed_url host** against the same setting. However, `Jobs::PollFeed` does not perform host validation at all (it just opens `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` and imports item links), and `TopicEmbed` only checks URL format (`/^https?\:\/\//`) and does not validate host. So the claim that host-validation logic is duplicated across EmbedController, TopicRetriever, PollFeed, and TopicEmbed is not accurate, and the “will drift” concern is speculative/maintainability-focused rather than a concrete defect evidenced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever synchronously executes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}), bypassing Sidekiq and coupling the retriever to the poller's internals; should use Jobs.enqueue or extracted shared logic

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly instead of enqueuing it. However, `TopicRetriever` itself is invoked from the background job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (enqueued by `EmbedController`), so this call still runs inside Sidekiq execution context rather than in a web request. Calling another job class’ `execute` method directly is a design/architecture concern (coupling) but is not a verifiable defect (bug/security/correctness issue) introduced by the diff on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic Redis setnx/expire in TopicRetriever can leave a key with no TTL if the process dies between calls, permanently wedging retrieval for that embed URL; should use SET key val EX 60 NX

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses two separate Redis calls: `setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes (or the request is interrupted) after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will exist without a TTL. Subsequent calls will see `setnx` fail and return `true` (retrieved recently), so retrieval for that specific embed URL can be blocked indefinitely. Using an atomic `SET key value NX EX 60` (or a transaction/Lua) would prevent this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: Jobs::PollFeed#feed_key and its require 'digest/sha1' are never called

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `require 'digest/sha1'` is only used by the `feed_key` method. Within the diff, `feed_key` is never referenced: `execute` conditionally calls `poll_feed`, and `poll_feed` parses the feed and imports items without calling `feed_key` or using any SHA1-based key. No other added/modified code calls `Jobs::PollFeed#feed_key`, so both the method and its digest require are currently unused (dead code) as introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead locale key embed.permalink is added but never referenced by any view or JS

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `embed.permalink` under `config/locales/server.en.yml`, but the only new I18n lookups in the added views/models reference `embed.title`, `embed.start_discussion`, `embed.continue`, `embed.loading`, and `embed.imported_from`. There is no reference to `embed.permalink` in the new JS (`embed.js`), views (`embed/*.erb`), or Ruby code shown. However, an unused locale string is a maintenance nit/bloat rather than a functional bug or correctness defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import mutates its contents argument in place with <<, a hidden side effect on a public model API

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the method appends an “Imported from” footer via `contents << "\n<hr>..."`, which mutates the caller-provided `contents` String in place. Since `.import` is a public class method and takes `contents` as an argument, this introduces a hidden side effect: any code that keeps a reference to the original string will see it modified after calling `.import`. This behavior is directly present in the diff and is not merely stylistic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import bakes the localized footer HTML into content_sha1, so translation changes trigger mass rewrites of embedded posts and the hash no longer represents source content; the unescaped URL interpolation is also an injection point

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends a localized HTML footer to `contents` before computing `content_sha1`: ```rb contents << "...#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")}..." content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents) ``` This means the SHA1 is not a hash of just the source article/feed content; it also includes the current translation string. If the locale text changes (or varies by locale during imports), subsequent polls/imports will compute a different SHA1 for otherwise-identical source content and will trigger unnecessary `PostRevisor` updates. Additionally, `url` is interpolated directly into an HTML attribute with single quotes and into link text without escaping/sanitization. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other HTML-breaking characters in the URL. Because these imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` (bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline), this becomes a verifiable XSS/injection risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Already-applied migrations edited in the same PR (whitespace/newline changes and force: true added to create_top_topics), causing schema divergence and silent table drops on replay
Weak postMessage origin check in embed.js uses substring indexOf match instead of strict origin comparison
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same security flaw: origin validation relies on a substring/indexOf check rather than strict origin equality, allowing bypass with attacker-controlled domains that contain the trusted domain string (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com).

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js dereferences document.getElementById('discourse-comments') without a null check, throwing on pages where the div is missing

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the code assigns `comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If the element with id `discourse-comments` is not present in the DOM, `comments` will be null and this will throw a runtime error. There is no null/undefined guard before dereferencing `comments`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `force: true` added to already-shipped migration create_top_topics, causing destructive DROP TABLE re-run risk

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will DROP the table if it already exists before creating it. While migrations normally run once, this change makes re-running or executing the migration against a DB where `top_topics` already exists (e.g., inconsistent schema_migrations state, manual table present, or accidental rerun in some environments) destructive, where previously it would have failed instead of dropping data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `force: true` on new topic_embeds table converts 'already exists' error into silent data destruction on re-run

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it, rather than raising an error. That means if this migration is ever executed against a database that already has a `topic_embeds` table (e.g., due to a misapplied/partial migration history, manual table creation, or other environments), it can silently destroy existing data. This behavior matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: NOT NULL column with default added to large posts table without concurrency safeguards, causing table rewrite and ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock downtime

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` with `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions common at the time this code was written, adding a NOT NULL column with a non-NULL default rewrites the entire table and takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on `posts` for the duration, which can cause downtime on large installations. The migration includes no phased/backfill approach or concurrency safeguards (e.g., add nullable column, backfill in batches, then add default/constraint).

adjudication_records.issue_text: content_sha1 updated unconditionally even when revision fails, permanently losing content updates for feed imports

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed is found and `content_sha1` differs, it calls `revisor.revise!(user, ...)` and then **always** executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` without checking whether the revision actually succeeded (`revise!` can return `false` when `should_revise?` is false, e.g., user not allowed to edit / edit window expired, etc.). Because `update_column` bypasses validations/callbacks and is unconditional, the embed record can be marked as up-to-date even if the post content was not updated, preventing future re-import attempts for that change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feed items without content crash the entire poll_feed job, skipping all remaining items

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item has no `content` (i.e., `i.content` is `nil`, which is common for many RSS feeds that only provide `description`/`summary`), calling `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, causing the `poll_feed` execution to abort and skip processing the remaining items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Double-HTML-decoding of feed content with raw_html cook method enables raw HTML injection into posts
Non-atomic SETNX/EXPIRE throttle in topic_retriever can permanently blacklist an embed URL if process dies between calls

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle does `if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two separate Redis commands, not atomic. If the process crashes (or loses Redis connection) after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE executes, the key can be left without a TTL, causing `setnx` to fail forever on future calls and making `retrieved_recently?` always return true for that embed URL (effectively a permanent throttle/blacklist for that URL).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript in embed layout, allowing broken JS or script injection
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying vulnerability: the unescaped request.referer header is inserted into inline JavaScript without proper escaping, enabling JavaScript injection/XSS if the referer is attacker-controlled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of --category option from Disqus import is a breaking interface change with no deprecation path

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the Thor CLI option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes all associated logic that looked up `category_id` and passed it into `PostCreator` (`category: category_id`). The import path is also changed to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)`, which does not accept or apply a category. This is a concrete, verifiable removal of a previously supported command-line interface/feature, and any existing scripts or docs using `--category` will now fail with an unknown option and/or lose categorization behavior, with no compatibility shim or deprecation shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed#feed_key is dead code — no ETag/Last-Modified conditional-GET tracking implemented

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` is defined to generate a Redis key based on the feed URL (`"feed-modified:#{...}"`), implying intent to track last-modified/ETag state. However, `feed_key` is never referenced within `PollFeed` (or elsewhere in the diff), and `poll_feed` always does an unconditional `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no conditional-GET headers or Redis storage. So `feed_key` is currently unused/dead code and no ETag/Last-Modified tracking is implemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: Post#cook returns raw verbatim when cook_method == raw_html, and TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method: raw_html from unsanitized feed content, rendered via <%= raw post.cooked %> in the embed view

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an explicit bypass of the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` using `contents` from feeds/remote pages (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` uses `SimpleRSS.parse` then `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`), and `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `href`/`src` without removing scripts/event handlers. In the embed UI, the content is rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and the provided spec asserts `post.cooked == post.raw`, confirming the unsanitized HTML is stored/rendered. Therefore, untrusted/compromised feed content can result in stored XSS executing in the embed iframe on the Discourse origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed only does CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) with no tag filtering or attribute stripping, and unescapeHTML re-animates correctly escaped payloads like <script> into live markup before storing raw

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, feed item content is set to `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passed into `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post via `PostCreator` with `skip_validations: true` and `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` returns `raw` directly (skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore any HTML coming from the RSS/Atom feed (including content that was HTML-escaped like `<script>` and then reactivated by `unescapeHTML`) can become live markup stored and rendered, with no tag/attribute filtering in this path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HTML/attribute injection in the 'imported from' footer: url is interpolated into a single-quoted HTML attribute with no escaping; the /^https?\:\/\// guard is trivially bypassed by payloads like http://evil.com/' onmouseover='alert(1)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In TopicEmbed.import, the code appends an HTML footer containing an anchor built via string interpolation: `"#{url}"` (passed as `link:` to `I18n.t`). The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which only checks the prefix and does not prevent quotes or other HTML-breaking characters. A URL like `http://evil.com/' onmouseover='alert(1)` still matches the regex and will break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute, enabling attribute/HTML injection. Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (skipping sanitization), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, making this a stored XSS vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed crashes on feeds lacking content:encoded (plain RSS description-only or many Atom feeds) because i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError, with no fallback to i.description/i.summary
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: calling `i.content.scrub` assumes `i.content` exists, but many feeds omit `content`/`content:encoded`, causing a NoMethodError/nil crash. Both recommend falling back to `description` (candidate also mentions `summary`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No per-item rescue in PollFeed's rss.items.each: the first malformed entry aborts the loop, so items after it are silently skipped every hour with retry: false and no logging

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `rss.items.each do |i| ... content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) ... TopicEmbed.import(...) end` with no per-item `rescue`. If any item has unexpected/nil fields (e.g., `i.content` is nil) or `TopicEmbed.import` raises, the exception will terminate the entire job and the remaining items in the feed won't be processed in that run. Because the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, Sidekiq won't retry the failed execution, so later items are skipped until the next scheduled run (and could be repeatedly skipped if the same bad item keeps causing an exception).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer-based validation in embed_controller is trivially spoofable, allowing anonymous users to hit /embed/best?embed_url=... for unlimited URLs, each enqueueing a RetrieveTopic job (job-queue flooding and request-amplification DoS against the embeddable host)

adjudication.rationale: The new EmbedController#best gates access solely on `request.referer` host matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (ensure_embeddable), which is a client-controlled header and can be trivially spoofed by non-browser clients. When `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, it unconditionally `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)`. There is no rate limiting on this endpoint or on enqueuing; TopicRetriever throttles only per exact `@embed_url` key, so an attacker can submit many distinct `embed_url` values (including even invalid URLs, which still enqueue jobs though they won't fetch) to flood the job queue. For valid URLs on the configured embeddable host, jobs will fetch remote content via `open(url).read`, enabling request amplification against that host as well.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SSRF in import_remote/PollFeed: open(url) follows redirects with no scheme/IP validation and no DNS rebinding protection, allowing rebinding to internal addresses (e.g., 169.254.169.254) and exfiltration via imported content
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe an SSRF risk in PollFeed due to calling open() on a configurable URL (feed_polling_url) without sufficient validation, enabling an attacker controlling that setting to make the server fetch arbitrary/internal URLs. The candidate adds extra details (redirects, scheme/IP checks, DNS rebinding), but it’s the same underlying issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No read timeout or response-size cap on remote fetches, so a slow-drip server can pin a Sidekiq worker indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple remote fetches using `open-uri` without any explicit timeouts or size limits. In `Jobs::PollFeed`, it does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, and in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` it does `open(url).read` (reading the entire response into memory) before passing it to Readability. These are run from Sidekiq jobs (`Jobs::PollFeed`, `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` via `TopicRetriever`), so a slow or streaming response (sending periodic small chunks) or a very large response can keep a worker busy for an unbounded duration and/or consume excessive memory. No read timeout configuration or response-size cap is present in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic SETNX+EXPIRE in TopicRetriever: if the process dies between setnx and expire, the key persists with no TTL forever, permanently blocking retrieval for that URL; should use atomic SET key val NX EX 60

adjudication.rationale:
In lib/topic_retriever.rb, retrieved_recently? uses a two-step pattern:

```ruby
if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")
  $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)
  return false
end
true
```

This is non-atomic. If the process/thread dies or raises after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key `retrieved:<embed_url>` will be left without a TTL. Future calls will see `setnx` fail and return `true`, causing retrieval to be throttled indefinitely for that specific URL. Using an atomic Redis command (e.g., `SET key val NX EX 60`) avoids this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: content_sha1 is updated via update_column even when revisor.revise! fails (return value ignored), silently marking the embed as synced when the post diverges from the source

adjudication.rationale:
In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed’s content changes, it does:

```rb
revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)
revisor.revise!(...)
embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)
```

The return value of `revise!` is ignored, and `update_column` will persist the new `content_sha1` regardless of whether `revise!` actually applied the change. From `PostRevisor#revise!` (shown in the diff), it explicitly returns `false` when `should_revise?` is false, so failure is a supported outcome. In that case, the embed record would be marked as having the new SHA while the post content was not updated, leaving the post diverged from the source but “synced” according to `content_sha1`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent no-op when embed_by_username doesn't resolve: both poll_feed and fetch_http do 'return if user.blank?' with no logging, so a typo'd username causes the system to run green while importing nothing

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code resolves the importing user via `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and then immediately `return if user.blank?` with no error/logging. Likewise, `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` does the same lookup and `return if user.blank?`. Since both callers only check that `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is present (not that it maps to an existing user), a typo or deleted user will cause feed polling / HTTP retrieval to silently do nothing while jobs still execute successfully.

adjudication_records.issue_text: loading.html.erb reloads the iframe every 30 seconds indefinitely even when retrieval can never succeed (host mismatch, unset embed_by_username, permanent fetch failure), creating an infinite job-churn amplifier

adjudication.rationale:
In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists for the given embed_url, it always enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... ) and renders embed/loading. loading.html.erb then unconditionally reloads the page every 30 seconds. On each reload, #best runs again, still finds no embed, and enqueues another retrieve_topic job.

Retrieval can permanently never succeed for cases shown in the diff: e.g. TopicRetriever#invalid_host? will prevent retrieval if URI(@embed_url).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host, yet the controller never checks this before enqueuing; also TopicRetriever#fetch_http can effectively fail if embed_by_username is unset/invalid (it calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase, which will error if nil). In these cases the loading page will reload indefinitely and repeatedly enqueue failing/no-op jobs, creating job churn/amplification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_url column is t.string (255 chars) with a unique index, but real-world URLs routinely exceed 255 characters, causing TopicEmbed.create! to raise and abort remaining PollFeed items

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` defines `embed_url` as `t.string` (typically `varchar(255)`) and adds a unique index on it. The code stores arbitrary external URLs into this column (`TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` from RSS/remote import) with no length validation or truncation. If a URL exceeds 255 characters, the insert/update will raise (e.g., Postgres “value too long for type character varying(255)”), and since `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` iterates `rss.items.each` without rescue, a single long URL can abort the job and prevent processing remaining items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dependency lock incomplete: only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated; the primary Gemfile.lock is not, so frozen-mode deployments or CI against the main lockfile will fail or miss the new gems

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` to `Gemfile` and updates `Gemfile_rails4.lock` accordingly, but it does not show whether a primary `Gemfile.lock` exists in this repo or is the lockfile used for deployments/CI. From the diff alone, it's not verifiable that there is a `Gemfile.lock` that should have been updated (it may be a Rails-4-specific bundle setup that only uses `Gemfile_rails4.lock`). Thus the claim about “frozen-mode deployments or CI against the main lockfile” failing relies on repository context not present in the diff.
